question: According to the Delaware CDL manual, which trailer in a doubles/triples combination is most likely to turn over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
choice_a: All trailers are equally likely to turn over
choice_b: The first trailer directly behind the tractor
choice_c: The last trailer in the combination
explanation: The manual states that doubles and triples are more likely to turn over because of the crack-the-whip effect, and that the last trailer in a combination is most likely to turn over.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: What should a driver do to prevent trailers from rolling over when pulling doubles or triples?
choice_a: Maintain full highway speed through curves for stability
choice_b: Steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves
choice_c: Brake hard immediately before entering any curve
choice_d: Steer abruptly to counteract trailer sway
explanation: The manual states that to prevent trailers from rolling over, you must steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves, since a safe speed for a single trailer may be too fast for doubles or triples.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Why must drivers of doubles/triples allow more following distance than other commercial vehicle drivers?
choice_a: Federal law requires a fixed 500-foot following gap for all combination vehicles
choice_c: Doubles/triples take up more space, are longer, and cannot be turned or stopped as suddenly
choice_d: Doubles/triples have weaker brakes installed by manufacturers
explanation: The manual explains that doubles and triples take up more space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and can't be turned or stopped suddenly, so drivers should allow more following distance.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Per the manual, why is extra caution needed when driving doubles/triples in bad weather or mountain conditions?
choice_a: They are legally exempt from carrying tire chains
choice_b: They have greater length and more dead axles pulled by the drive axles, increasing the chance of skids and loss of traction
choice_c: Their trailer brakes are disabled automatically in wet weather
choice_d: They are not permitted to use cruise control
explanation: The manual states that in adverse conditions, double and triple bottoms have greater length and more dead axles to pull with the drive axles than other drivers, creating more chance for skids and loss of traction.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Converter dollies built on or after what date are required to have antilock braking systems, according to the manual?
explanation: The manual states that converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: How can a driver identify that a converter dolly is equipped with antilock brakes?
choice_a: It has a manufacturer sticker on the pintle hook
choice_b: It has a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly
choice_c: It has a green indicator light on the tongue
choice_d: It has a red reflective triangle on the rear
explanation: The manual states that converter dollies with antilock brakes will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: For the safest handling on the road, how should twin trailers be arranged behind the tractor?
choice_a: The more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in the first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear
choice_b: Both trailers must be loaded to identical weights before coupling
choice_c: The heaviest trailer should always be placed last
choice_d: The lighter trailer should always be positioned directly behind the tractor
explanation: The manual states that for the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in the first position behind the tractor, with the lighter trailer in the rear.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: If the second (rear) trailer does not have spring brakes, what should the driver do before coupling to help secure it?
choice_a: Apply the trolley valve to lock the trailer's service brakes
choice_b: Leave the trailer unsecured since it will be coupled within minutes
choice_c: Drive the tractor close to the trailer, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, then disconnect the emergency line to set the emergency brakes
choice_d: Immediately chock all wheels and skip connecting any air lines
explanation: The manual explains that if the second trailer lacks spring brakes, the driver should connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line to set the emergency brakes, chocking the wheels if there is any doubt.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: What is a converter dolly, as defined in the manual?
choice_a: A type of glad hand connector used on air lines
choice_b: A hydraulic lift used only to raise a trailer's landing gear
choice_c: A braking device installed exclusively on triple-trailer rigs
choice_d: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
explanation: The manual defines a converter gear on a dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, what must be true about the trailer height?
choice_a: It must be at least one foot higher than the fifth wheel
choice_b: It must be exactly level with the ground on all sides
choice_c: It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under
choice_d: Height does not matter as long as the landing gear is lowered
explanation: The manual states trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under it.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When making a visual check of the coupling between the dolly and the trailer, what should the driver confirm?
choice_a: There is no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel, and the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin
choice_b: The trailer tires are inflated to the manufacturer's recommended pressure
choice_c: The trailer's cargo doors are locked and sealed
choice_d: The safety chains are painted a visible color
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to make a visual check confirming no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and that the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: After connecting the converter dolly to the rear trailer and opening the shut-off valves, how should the driver verify air reaches the trailer brakes?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake and listen for a hissing sound at the front bumper
choice_b: Rev the engine and check the fuel gauge reading
choice_c: Disconnect the electrical cord and test the brake lights
choice_d: Push the "air supply" knob in to charge the trailer brakes, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off
explanation: The manual states to charge trailer brakes by pushing the air supply knob in, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: What is one of the first steps when uncoupling the rear trailer of a twin-trailer rig?
choice_a: Remove the landing gear entirely from the trailer
choice_b: Release the pintle hook immediately upon stopping
choice_c: Disconnect the kingpin before parking the rig
choice_d: Park the rig in a straight line on firm, level ground and apply the parking brakes
explanation: The manual's uncoupling procedure begins with parking the rig in a straight line on firm level ground and applying the parking brakes so the rig won't move.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: What danger does the manual warn about if a driver unlocks the pintle hook while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: The kingpin will become permanently bent
choice_b: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling very difficult
choice_c: The tractor will immediately lose all air pressure
choice_d: The trailer's service brakes will automatically release
explanation: The manual warns to never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When a set of doubles or triples is properly connected, what position should the shut-off valve be in at the rear of the last trailer?
explanation: The manual's inspection checklist specifies that the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED, while the valve at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

topic: Checking Air Flow to All Trailers
question: When checking that air flows to all trailers, what should the driver do at the rear of the last trailer to confirm the system is charged?
choice_a: Disconnect the electrical cord and check for sparks
choice_b: Remove the landing gear crank handle
choice_c: Open the emergency line shut-off valve and listen for escaping air
choice_d: Loosen the kingpin and check for movement
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to go to the rear of the rig and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer, listening for escaping air to confirm the entire system is charged.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4

question: During the tractor protection valve test, within what pressure range does the manual say the trailer air supply control usually pops out to the "emergency" position?
choice_a: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
choice_b: Usually within the range of 60 to 90 psi
choice_d: Usually within the range of 5 to 10 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out when the air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4

question: How does a driver test that the trailer service brakes are connected and working, per the manual?
choice_a: Check the tire tread depth on all trailer axles
choice_b: Release the parking brakes, move the vehicle forward slowly, and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve), feeling for the brakes to come on
choice_c: Disconnect the trailer and visually inspect the brake shoes
choice_d: Press the foot brake pedal while parked and listen for air leaks
explanation: The manual describes testing trailer service brakes by releasing the parking brakes, moving forward slowly, and applying the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve) to feel that they come on.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-4
